penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Optimizing and delivering a Windows bare-metal image is hands-on technical work — running sysprep, MDT/WDS pipelines, testing deployments — that cannot be automated end-to-end by Claude. Each customer engagement requires real system access and manual validation.

penalties_applied.name: requires_synchronous_human
penalties_applied.reason: MSP and enterprise IT buyers expect scoping calls, environment-specific consultation, and handoff sessions before trusting a custom image pipeline — live interaction is effectively required to close and deliver.

rationale: The buyers — IT ops engineers and MSPs — are real and have budget, but this is fundamentally a hands-on technical services problem: producing a slimmed Windows image requires direct access to the target environment, toolchain-specific configuration (MDT, WDS, WIM tooling), and iterative testing that Claude cannot perform autonomously. Operational_autonomy scores 2 and buildability_with_ai scores 3, both far below build_gate floors, and penalties for per-customer manual work push the total to 2.3. This is a consulting engagement, not a factory-deliverable micro-service.
solution_plan: Not viable for this factory. A solo non-technical operator cannot build or maintain a Windows image optimization service without direct system access, environment-specific tooling knowledge, and hands-on testing per client. Even framed as a guide or checklist product, the competitive landscape (free Microsoft documentation, DISM tools, MDT community) makes monetization implausible. Drop and redirect attention to software-deliverable opportunities.
notes: Failing build_gates: operational_autonomy (scored 2, floor 7), buildability_with_ai (scored 3, floor 6). Penalties for requires_human_fulfillment and requires_synchronous_human compound the disqualification. Drop.
